output: Probability-like score that the site of a hostname (its registrable-domain approximation) looks like a tracking/analytics site from public blocklists. A DNS lookup is an attempt to contact a host, not proof that data was sent; the score never creates a finding on its own.

featureSpace.site: last two labels, or last three when the second-to-last label is one of secondLevel and the last label has two letters
featureSpace.ngrams: distinct character n-grams of length 2-5 of '^' + host + '$'
featureSpace.hash: FNV-1a 32-bit over the UTF-8 bytes of each n-gram, bucket = hash & (2^hashBits - 1); a bucket counts once

dense.entropy: Shannon entropy of the characters in bits / 5

thresholdRule: Maximises F1 on out-of-fold predictions of the training split (5-fold CV grouped by registrable domain).

metrics.evaluation: Held-out 20% split by domain family (no family in both train and test); sites, not full hostnames

trainingData.name: EasyPrivacy
trainingData.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later OR CC BY-SA 3.0 (or later); used under CC BY-SA 3.0

limits: Labels mirror blocklist editors' choices; a list host can be multi-purpose and a missing host is not proof it is clean.
Only the site is scored; first-party tracking subdomains (e.g. metrics.<shop>.com) are out of scope for this model.
Negatives are popular sites; obscure legitimate sites are under-represented, so expect more false positives on them than the test FPR shows.
Lists change daily; new tracker domains and first-party CNAME cloaking can look like ordinary hosts.
Hashed n-grams collide, so the per-n-gram explanation is approximate.
